newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan traders see CBOT soy prices in range.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan traders see CBOT soy prices in range.

text.p: Soybean prices will hold in a range of US$8.50-US$9.00 per bushel following Monday's sharp fall on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT), Taiwan traders said on Tuesday.
"Soybean prices are likely to flow between the $8.50 to $9.00 range in the near term," one said.
CBOT soybean futures dropped on Monday after the U.S. Department of Agriculture pegged its 1996/97 soybean ending stocks unchanged at 125 million bushels.
The CBOT soybean July contract fell 20-1/2 U.S. cents to end at US$8.68-1/2 a bushel.
Taiwan soybean buyers said the sharp fall in soybean and soymeal prices in Chicago was a technical correction to a recent rally.
"The big drop on CBOT is only a correction, which is normal after a rally," an oilseeds buyer at Taiwan's Hui Shung Corp said.

Local buyers recently pared soybean purchases after the outbreak of a hog epidemic began hitting the island's edible oil producers. The fall in demand for soy-based feed has forced buyers to reduce imports.
Taiwan has slaughtered millions of pigs since March 20, when the Council of Agriculture announced the foot and mouth epidemic and banned pork exports.

Council data showed the deadly virus had been detected on 5,501 of Taiwan's 25,000 hog farms, with official projections showing that 4.39 million of the island's 14 million pigs would have to be destroyed.
The farm council announced on Thursday that the epidemic appeared to be under control.
